title: Semi-analytic Inference of Satellite Densities in the Cold Dark Matter Model Part I. Comparison to Ultra-faint Dwarf Kinematics
comment: 22+11 pages, 8+6 figures, video abstract at https://youtu.be/dal8_lRz3EI
summary: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies are critical testing grounds for probing the limits of galaxy formation in the cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm. Employing a semi-analytic cosmological satellite generator that captures the expected CDM halo population, we estimate Milky Way dwarf density profiles through two methods: a kinematic approach using stellar velocity dispersions and a separate method based on dwarf stellar masses. The kinematic approach yields a larger diversity in central dark matter densities than expected from the CDM population, as inferred from the stellar-to-halo mass relation, with compact ultra-faints appearing overdense and larger systems appearing underdense. For the ultra-faint dwarfs with at least 10 stars with spectroscopic measurements, this discrepancy persists at the ~2.4$σ$ level across all considered systematic variations on the semi-analytic modeling. Our framework introduces a novel, robust procedure for testing the consistency of the observed population of Milky Way satellites with cosmological expectations. As future surveys discover new dwarf satellites and refine stellar velocity measurements, updating this analysis will provide an increasingly stringent test of the CDM paradigm.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a semi-analytic cosmological satellite generator to model Milky Way ultra-faint dwarf galaxies within the CDM paradigm. Comparing kinematic density estimates (from stellar velocity dispersions) against stellar mass-based expectations reveals a ~2.4σ discrepancy in central dark matter densities, with compact ultra-faints appearing overdense and larger systems underdense. The framework offers a robust test of CDM predictions against observed dwarf populations.
AI.motivation: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies provide critical tests of the cold dark matter paradigm by probing the extremes of galaxy formation. The authors aim to determine whether the observed diversity in Milky Way dwarf central densities is consistent with CDM halo population expectations.
AI.method: The authors employ a semi-analytic cosmological satellite generator that captures the expected CDM halo population. They estimate Milky Way dwarf density profiles via two approaches: (1) a kinematic method using stellar velocity dispersions, and (2) a method based on dwarf stellar masses. They then compare these density estimates to CDM expectations.
AI.result: The kinematic approach reveals larger diversity in central dark matter densities than predicted by the CDM population, with compact ultra-faints appearing overdense and larger systems underdense. For ultra-faint dwarfs with at least 10 spectroscopic stars, the discrepancy persists at ~2.4σ confidence across all considered systematic variations in the semi-analytic modeling.
AI.conclusion: The framework introduces a novel, robust procedure for testing the consistency of observed Milky Way satellite populations with cosmological expectations. Future surveys discovering new dwarf satellites and refining stellar velocity measurements will provide increasingly stringent tests of the CDM paradigm through this analysis.

title: Superdiffusion at the Galactic Centre
comment: Submitted
summary: Tracking S-star cluster orbits around Sgr A* calibrates orbital transport models for space-borne gravitational wave detectors. Standard kinetic theories model this cluster via local Fokker-Planck equations, which predict that general relativistic precession halts angular momentum diffusion at the Schwarzschild barrier. Because inverse-square gravitational encounters generate a Holtsmark torque distribution with infinite variance, resonant relaxation operates as a space-fractional process governed by non-local Lévy flights. We simulate this superdiffusive continuous-time random walk using a Markov chain initialized with empirical S-star orbits, including the recently observd S301. Integro-differential fractional operators allow trajectories to cross regions of quenched local diffusion without density buildup at the barrier. Non-equilibrium regimes yield immediate linear flux growth, while secular tidal heating at periastron inflates stellar radii to shift disruption boundaries. Regularized backward integration of the fractional transport equation traces current phase space configurations back to initial deposition states, matching the energy requirements of the \emph{Fermi} bubbles. Relativistic precession does not suppress mass-ratio inspiral rates, which provides a model for event topologies in target galactic nuclei.

AI.tldr: The paper models S-star cluster orbits around Sgr A* using a space-fractional superdiffusive continuous-time random walk governed by Lévy flights, rather than local Fokker-Planck equations, to capture the Schwarzschild barrier crossing, tidal disruption, and inspiral dynamics relevant to space-borne gravitational wave detectors.
AI.motivation: Standard local Fokker-Planck kinetic theories predict that general relativistic precession halts angular momentum diffusion at the Schwarzschild barrier, which fails to fully capture the dynamics of S-star orbits around Sgr A*. A more accurate calibration of orbital transport models is needed for space-borne gravitational wave detectors.
AI.method: The authors treat resonant relaxation as a space-fractional process using integro-differential fractional operators, motivated by the Holtsmark torque distribution's infinite variance from inverse-square gravitational encounters. They simulate a superdiffusive continuous-time random walk (Markov chain) initialized with empirical S-star orbits including the recently observed S301, and use regularized backward integration of the fractional transport equation.
AI.result: Lévy flights allow trajectories to cross regions of quenched local diffusion without density buildup at the barrier. Non-equilibrium regimes show immediate linear flux growth, and secular tidal heating at periastron inflates stellar radii, shifting disruption boundaries. Backward integration reproduces initial deposition states matching Fermi bubble energy requirements, and relativistic precession does not suppress mass-ratio inspiral rates, providing a model for event topologies in galactic nuclei.
AI.conclusion: Fractional, non-local kinetic transport provides a more accurate framework than standard local Fokker-Planck theory for S-star cluster dynamics around Sgr A*, with implications for gravitational wave event rates and nuclear galactic phenomena.

title: The influence of feedback on the baryonic content of haloes in the COLIBRE simulations
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: We present predictions for the relation between the halo gas mass fraction and halo mass, $f_{\rm gas}^{200}-M_{200}$, from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation, and explore how the gas content of haloes is influenced by feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei (AGN) over time. The $f_{\rm gas}^{200}-M_{200}$ relation in COLIBRE is non-monotonic, with a peak at $M_{200}\sim 10^{11.5-12}$~M$_\odot$. Below this mass, feedback from supernovae efficiently expels gas from the haloes of dwarf galaxies, and above it, AGN feedback efficiently depletes the haloes of galaxy groups. The fiducial COLIBRE model yields gas fractions for galaxy groups and clusters that agree with constraints from Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray data, but which are high relative to gas fractions inferred from eROSITA stacks and measurements of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel-dovich (kSZ) effect. COLIBRE's hybrid AGN feedback model, which combines thermal and jet-driven feedback, produces lower gas fractions in better agreement with eROSITA and kSZ measurements. COLIBRE produces lower gas fractions for groups and clusters than EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, and better agreement with observational constraints. We investigate the origin of this improvement relative to EAGLE, and how the resolution of the simulation affects the impact of feedback. Our results demonstrate that halo gas fractions are a sensitive probe of feedback physics, and that they can differ significantly between simulations that otherwise produce very similar galaxy populations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents predictions for the halo gas mass fraction-halo mass relation (fgas^200-M200) from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations, showing that this relation is non-monotonic with a peak at M200~10^11.5-12 Msun, shaped by supernova feedback (expelling gas from dwarf haloes below the peak) and AGN feedback (depleting gas from group haloes above it). COLIBRE's hybrid thermal+jet AGN feedback model produces gas fractions in better agreement with X-ray (Chandra, XMM-Newton) and SZ (eROSITA, kSZ) observations than EAGLE and other contemporary simulations.
AI.motivation: To understand how feedback from supernovae and AGN influences the gas content of dark matter haloes across cosmic time, and to test whether halo gas fractions can serve as a sensitive probe of feedback physics in galaxy formation simulations.
AI.method: The study uses the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation and analyzes the fgas^200-M200 relation, comparing the fiducial model against a hybrid AGN feedback model (combining thermal and jet-driven feedback) and against earlier simulations like EAGLE, as well as against observational constraints from X-ray (Chandra, XMM-Newton) and SZ (eROSITA, kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich) data. The resolution dependence of feedback impact is also investigated.
AI.result: The fgas^200-M200 relation is non-monotonic, peaking at M200~10^11.5-12 Msun. The fiducial COLIBRE model matches X-ray constraints for groups and clusters but overpredicts gas fractions relative to eROSITA and kSZ measurements. The hybrid AGN feedback model lowers gas fractions to better agreement with eROSITA and kSZ data. COLIBRE yields lower gas fractions for groups/clusters than EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, with better agreement to observations. Halo gas fractions are shown to differ significantly between simulations that otherwise produce very similar galaxy populations.
AI.conclusion: Halo gas fractions are a sensitive and discriminating probe of feedback physics. COLIBRE's hybrid AGN feedback model improves agreement with observational constraints over previous simulations like EAGLE, demonstrating that gas content in haloes is a powerful diagnostic that can distinguish between feedback implementations even when galaxy populations look similar.

title: An Exploratory Analysis of New Large Gaia-informed Quasar Samples in SDSS-V
comment: Resubmitted to ApJ on 28 July 2026 after addressing the referee report. The data will be available in SDSS-V/DR20
summary: Quasars are luminous objects that provide insights into the physics and evolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and their accretion flows, galaxy evolution, and even cosmology. In this study, we present an exploratory study based on the ongoing fifth generation of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS-V) and its unique dual-hemisphere, wide-field, and multi-object spectroscopic capabilities, with the aim of creating a comprehensive, all-sky quasar sample. The targets were selected through two novel methods, GUA and Skewt-QSO, that rely primarily on data from WISE and Gaia, aiming to address gaps in previous large quasar samples. Our sample includes over 250,000 spectroscopically confirmed quasars reaching z~5, with tens of thousands of newly identified quasars in the southern hemisphere. The selection methods are highly pure, with well over 80% of the spectra collected being genuine quasars; the main contaminants are M-type stars. The detailed spectral decomposition procedure we employed shows that the quasars in the sample span a wide range of luminosities (Lbol~$10^{44}-10^{48} erg s^{-1}$), SMBH masses (MBH~$10^6-10^{10}$ Msun), and accretion rates (L/LEdd~0.01-1). The distributions of these properties are consistent with those of previous quasar catalogs, which are based on past generations of SDSS, once we account for potential selection biases related to the various survey depths. Our findings confirm that novel selection methods based on optical+IR colors and/or astrometry can yield a large, high-purity quasar sample over wide sky areas, including in cases where more nuanced multi-band photometry and/or multi-wavelength data in the X-ray or radio is not available. This SDSS-V sample, which will continue to grow, establishes a robust reference for future southern (time-domain) surveys, while enhancing and complementing our understanding of quasar demographics and SMBH evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an exploratory study using SDSS-V's dual-hemisphere spectroscopic capabilities to build a comprehensive all-sky quasar sample. Using two novel selection methods (GUA and Skewt-QSO) based primarily on WISE and Gaia data, the authors assembled over 250,000 spectroscopically confirmed quasars reaching z~5, with tens of thousands of new southern-hemisphere discoveries. The selection methods achieve >80% purity, and the quasars span wide ranges in luminosity, SMBH mass, and accretion rate consistent with previous SDSS-based catalogs after accounting for selection biases.
AI.motivation: To address gaps in previous large quasar samples—particularly in the southern hemisphere—and to create a comprehensive all-sky quasar catalog using novel selection methods that work even without multi-wavelength (X-ray/radio) data, leveraging SDSS-V's unique dual-hemisphere, wide-field, multi-object spectroscopic capabilities.
AI.method: Target selection uses two novel methods, GUA and Skewt-QSO, which rely primarily on WISE and Gaia data (optical+IR colors and/or astrometry). This is followed by spectroscopic confirmation with SDSS-V and detailed spectral decomposition to derive physical properties including bolometric luminosity, SMBH mass, and Eddington ratio.
AI.result: The sample contains over 250,000 spectroscopically confirmed quasars up to z~5, including tens of thousands of newly identified quasars in the southern hemisphere. Selection methods achieve >80% purity with M-type stars being the main contaminants. The quasars span Lbol~10^44-10^48 erg s^-1, MBH~10^6-10^10 Msun, and L/LEdd~0.01-1, with distributions consistent with previous SDSS quasar catalogs after accounting for selection biases.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that novel selection methods based on optical+IR colors and/or astrometry can yield large, high-purity quasar samples over wide sky areas, even without X-ray or radio data. This SDSS-V sample establishes a robust reference for future southern time-domain surveys and enhances understanding of quasar demographics and SMBH evolution.

title: Non-linear Evolution of Dark Plasma Subhalos
comment: 13+3 pages, 4+2 figures. Code available at https://github.com/aprabhu94/dark-plasma-subhalos
summary: Dark matter that self interacts through long-range forces exhibits coherent, collective effects that are absent in short-range interactions. In the case where dark matter interacts through a hidden-photon mediator, its dynamics closely resemble those of Standard Model plasmas. In such models, various astrophysical environments, including cluster collisions and subhalos orbiting their host halo, are susceptible to plasma instabilities: processes that modify the dark matter velocity distribution and lead to exponential growth of dark electromagnetic fields. In this paper, we present the first study of the non-linear evolution of electrostatic instabilities in dark matter subhalos orbiting within the Milky Way potential using a suite of particle-in-cell simulations. We find that the growth and saturation of these instabilities produce substantial turbulent heating and mass loss, with an efficiency that depends sensitively on subhalo mass and orbital eccentricity. For highly eccentric orbits, plasma heating can reduce the initial mass of a $10^7$ ($10^9$) $\text{M}_\odot$ subhalo by as much as $\sim 97\%$ ($\sim 84\%$) soon after first pericenter. Plasma-induced heating and stripping may therefore leave observable signatures in the Milky Way subhalo population, including a suppression of the low-mass subhalo mass function.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first particle-in-cell simulation study of the non-linear evolution of electrostatic plasma instabilities in dark matter subhalos orbiting within the Milky Way potential, for dark matter interacting via a hidden-photon mediator. The instabilities produce significant turbulent heating and mass loss, reducing the mass of 10^7 M_sun subhalos by up to ~97% and 10^9 M_sun subhalos by up to ~84% on highly eccentric orbits shortly after first pericenter, potentially leaving observable signatures in the Milky Way subhalo mass function.
AI.motivation: Dark matter with self-interactions through long-range forces (hidden-photon mediators) behaves like a plasma and is susceptible to plasma instabilities in astrophysical environments such as cluster collisions and subhalos orbiting within host halos. Previous work has not studied the non-linear evolution of these instabilities, so their full impact on dark matter subhalo structure is unknown.
AI.method: A suite of particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations is used to study the non-linear evolution of electrostatic instabilities in dark matter subhalos orbiting within the Milky Way potential. The simulations vary subhalo mass and orbital eccentricity to map the dependence of instability-driven heating and mass loss on these parameters.
AI.result: The growth and saturation of electrostatic instabilities produce substantial turbulent heating and mass loss, with efficiency depending sensitively on subhalo mass and orbital eccentricity. On highly eccentric orbits, plasma heating reduces the initial mass of 10^7 M_sun subhalos by up to ~97% and 10^9 M_sun subhalos by up to ~84%, occurring soon after first pericenter passage.
AI.conclusion: Plasma-induced heating and stripping from these instabilities may leave observable signatures in the Milky Way subhalo population, including a suppression of the low-mass subhalo mass function. This has implications for probing self-interacting dark matter models with long-range forces through galactic-scale observations.

title: Exploring the Limits of Spectral Line Stacking in Spectral Line Data and Application Toward the Detection of Bulk $^{13}$C Enrichment of Aromatics in TMC-1
summary: The formation history of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the interstellar medium remains a topic of active debate, with proposed mechanisms ranging from high-temperature stellar ejecta processes to low-temperature chemistry within molecular clouds. Recently, the identification of small PAHs in the cold, dark cloud TMC-1 has provided some circumstantial evidence of the latter. If these are formed in situ, their isotopic ratios, particularly $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, should reflect the local, bulk material of the molecular cloud; in contrast, PAHs formed in the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars may show enhanced $^{13}$C abundances. The expected radio signals of these $^{13}$C substituted species will be faint, and thus we conducted a detailed proof-of-concept analysis examining whether spectral line stacking and matched filtering techniques can robustly retrieve signal from multiple singly substituted $^{13}$C isotopologues in aggregate. We find that while retrieved signal decreases in the limit of spectral line confusion, false-positive detections are exceedingly improbable at the adopted 5$σ$ matched filter response detection threshold. We then demonstrate the technique on actual observational data of isotopologues of HC$_9$N toward TMC-1. Finally, we show using synthetic data that if laboratory rotational spectra of all singly substituted $^{13}$C isotopologues of cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene isomers existed, current observations of TMC-1 would be sensitive enough to discriminate between a local, bulk $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio and one with an enhanced $^{13}$C abundance suggestive of inheritance.

AI.tldr: This paper explores whether spectral line stacking and matched filtering can detect faint 13C-substituted PAH isotopologues in cold molecular clouds to distinguish between in-situ formation versus stellar inheritance. Using proof-of-concept analysis, actual TMC-1 observations of HC9N isotopologues, and synthetic data, the authors find the technique robustly retrieves signal with negligible false-positive rates at a 5σ threshold, and that current observations could discriminate formation scenarios for PAHs like cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene if their laboratory spectra were available.
AI.motivation: The formation history of PAHs in the interstellar medium is debated—whether they form via high-temperature stellar ejecta or low-temperature molecular cloud chemistry. Detecting small PAHs in the cold cloud TMC-1 suggests possible in-situ formation. Isotopic ratios, particularly 12C/13C, could discriminate between these scenarios: locally formed PAHs would reflect the cloud's bulk ratio, while those inherited from evolved stars may show enhanced 13C. However, expected radio signals from 13C-substituted species are faint, motivating the need for a robust detection technique.
AI.method: The authors conducted a proof-of-concept analysis using spectral line stacking and matched filtering techniques to retrieve signal from multiple singly substituted 13C isotopologues aggregated together. They tested the method's robustness limits under spectral line confusion, validated it on actual observational data of HC9N isotopologues toward TMC-1, and used synthetic data to assess sensitivity for discriminating between local bulk and enhanced 13C ratios for potential cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene isotopologue detections.
AI.result: Signal retrieval decreases in the limit of spectral line confusion, but false-positive detections are exceedingly improbable at the adopted 5σ matched filter response detection threshold. The technique was successfully demonstrated on observational data of HC9N isotopologues toward TMC-1. Synthetic data analysis shows that if laboratory rotational spectra of all singly substituted 13C isotopologues of cyanonaphthalene and cyanopyrene were available, current TMC-1 observations could discriminate between a local bulk 12C/13C ratio and one with enhanced 13C suggestive of inheritance.
AI.conclusion: The spectral line stacking and matched filtering approach is a viable strategy for detecting faint 13C-substituted PAH isotopologues in cold clouds, with robust rejection of false positives. With complete laboratory spectra, current observational sensitivity could enable discrimination between in-situ formation and stellar inheritance of PAHs in TMC-1, offering a path to resolving the PAH formation debate.

title: Gravitational Waves as a Source of Large-Scale White Noise: New Constraints
comment: 16 pages 2 figures
summary: A stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background sources a shear in the flow of cosmic fluid which, through non-linear mode coupling, generates large-scale white noise (LSWN) in the kurvature density field. Building on the LSWN framework of our previous work, we derive the amplitude of this GW-induced LSWN and translate the observational non-detection of LSWN into bounds on the production redshift and density of gravity waves. In particular, a minimal constraint on gravity waves with $z=0$ density parameter $Ω_\mathrm{GW0}^*$ in frequency band $f_*$ generated at redshift $z_*$ must satisfy ${z_*}^2\,Ω_\mathrm{GW0}^*<5\times10^7\,(f_*/\mathrm{nHz})^{3/2}$. This, for example, precludes the gravity waves recently detected by pulsar timing arrays \cite{NANOGrav:2023hvm} from being present before $z_*\sim10^8$, long after the quark hadron phase transition. While orders of magnitude stronger than other constraints on gravity waves, this is a minimal LSWN constraint as realistic modeling of early universe gravity wave production, including the granularity of the gravity-wave sources and the LSWN produced by the associated acoustic waves would probably tighten this constraint by orders of magnitude.

AI.tldr: This paper derives constraints on stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds by showing that GWs generate large-scale white noise (LSWN) in the curvature density field through non-linear mode coupling. The authors derive a minimal bound requiring z*²Ω_GW0* < 5×10⁷ (f_*/nHz)^(3/2), which excludes the PTA-detected GWs from existing before z*~10⁸, and note that realistic modeling would tighten this constraint further.
AI.motivation: To use the non-linear coupling between stochastic gravitational waves and the cosmic fluid to place new, stringent constraints on the production redshift and density of gravity waves, leveraging the LSWN framework developed in prior work.
AI.method: Building on the LSWN framework, the authors derive the amplitude of GW-induced LSWN in the curvature density field via non-linear mode coupling between the GW-induced shear and cosmic fluid perturbations, then translate the observational non-detection of LSWN into bounds on GW production redshift and density.
AI.result: The derived minimal constraint is z*²Ω_GW0* < 5×10⁷ (f_*/nHz)^(3/2), which rules out the NANOGrav PTA-detected GW background existing before z*~10⁸, far after the quark-hadron phase transition. These bounds are orders of magnitude stronger than other GW constraints.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic GW backgrounds produce observable LSWN signatures that yield extremely strong constraints on early-universe GW production. While the present constraint is minimal, more realistic modeling of early-universe GW sources and associated acoustic waves would likely tighten it by orders of magnitude.

title: Cosmic Pairs: A DESI Census of Dual and Offset AGN as Precursors to Massive Black Hole Binaries
comment: 38 pages, 18 figures, 1 table. To be submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a systematic census of dual and offset active galactic nuclei (AGN) using spectroscopic data from the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). After correcting for observational systematics, our final sample contains $>7,000$ dual AGN and 27,000 galaxy pairs containing one AGN over the redshift range $0 \lesssim z \lesssim 3.6$. This sample expands the known dual AGN sample by $\sim 1-2$ orders of magnitude at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.4$, includes $\sim 50$ dwarf dual AGN candidates in a regime where only a handful were previously known, and triples the census at $z>2$. Dual AGN are preferentially found at small separations, consistent with merger-driven triggering of AGN activity. The two members of a pair differ in their star formation response: the more massive (primary) host changes little with separation, while the less massive (secondary) lies $\sim 0.3$ dex above matched inactive and one-AGN companions at the same projected separation in main-sequence offset. Using ASTRID simulations, we predict that the fraction of DESI dual AGN whose central black holes will merge by $z \sim 0$ increases with redshift, reaching $\sim 76\%$ by $z \sim 2$, while the fraction producing LISA-detectable mergers peaks at $\sim 37\%$ near $z \sim 0.9$. These results provide the largest uniformly selected spectroscopic sample of kpc-scale dual and offset AGN candidates from a single survey, connecting their host-galaxy and AGN demographics to the progenitor population of massive black hole mergers detectable by LISA.

AI.tldr: Using DESI DR1 spectroscopic data, the authors construct the largest uniformly selected census of >7,000 dual AGN and 27,000 one-AGN galaxy pairs across z~0-3.6, finding dual AGN preferentially at small separations (consistent with merger-driven triggering), distinct star formation offsets between primary and secondary hosts, and using ASTRID simulations to predict that up to ~76% of central black holes will merge by z~0 and ~37% will produce LISA-detectable mergers.
AI.motivation: To dramatically expand the known sample of dual and offset AGN (currently only a few hundred are known) and to connect their host-galaxy and AGN demographics to the progenitor population of massive black hole mergers detectable by LISA, building a statistically robust sample from a single homogeneous survey.
AI.method: The authors use spectroscopic data from DESI DR1 to systematically identify dual and offset AGN pairs. They correct for observational systematics to build a clean sample. They analyze projected separations and star formation main-sequence offsets (comparing primary vs. secondary hosts and against matched inactive/one-AGN companions). They use the ASTRID cosmological simulation to predict the fraction of black holes that will merge by z=0 and produce LISA-detectable mergers as a function of source redshift.
AI.result: The final sample contains >7,000 dual AGN and 27,000 one-AGN pairs over 0<z<3.6, expanding the known sample by 1-2 orders of magnitude at z~0.2-0.4, including ~50 dwarf dual AGN candidates, and tripling the census at z>2. Dual AGN are preferentially found at small separations. The secondary host lies ~0.3 dex above matched companions in main-sequence offset while the primary shows little change. ASTRID predicts the black-hole merger fraction increases with source redshift reaching ~76% by z~2, with LISA-detectable merger fraction peaking at ~37% near z~0.9.
AI.conclusion: The work provides the largest uniformly selected spectroscopic sample of kpc-scale dual and offset AGN candidates from a single survey, offering strong statistical evidence for merger-driven AGN triggering and connecting dual AGN demographics to the expected progenitor population of massive black hole mergers detectable by LISA.

title: DESI DR2 Results IV: Alcock-Paczyński Measurements from the Lyman Alpha Forest and Cosmological Constraints
summary: We present Alcock-Paczyński (AP) measurements from the full shape of Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest correlation functions measured from the second data release (DR2) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Our measurements include information from the Ly$α$ forest auto-correlation and its cross-correlation with quasars. We constrain the AP effect with $1\%$ precision at an effective redshift $z_\mathrm{eff}=2.33$, which is twice as tight as the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) constraint from the same data. When using the joint Ly$α$ AP and BAO results, we measure the ratios $D_\text{H}(z_\mathrm{eff})/r_\text{d}=8.600 \pm 0.066$ and $D_\text{M}(z_\mathrm{eff})/r_\text{d}=39.32 \pm 0.33$, where $D_\text{M}$ is the transverse comoving distance, $D_\text{H}$ is the Hubble distance, and $r_\text{d}$ is the sound horizon at the drag epoch. Assuming $Λ$CDM, Ly$α$ forest measurements combined with a nucleosynthesis prior produce a constraint on the Hubble constant $H_0=66.5\pm1.3\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. The Ly$α$ AP result corresponds to a matter fraction constraint $Ω_\text{m}=0.325\pm0.018$ in $Λ$CDM, which is $1.4σ$ higher than DESI BAO. This impacts the DESI results relative to the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), slightly reducing their discrepancy from $2.4σ$ to $2.2σ$. We present updated constraints on extended models using the joint DESI DR2 BAO and Ly$α$ forest full shape data, together with external data sets. When considering a time-evolving dark energy equation of state parametrized by $w_0$ and $w_a$, we find it is preferred over $Λ$CDM at $2.7σ$ for the combination of DESI and CMB data, and at $3.2σ$ when also including supernovae. With the new Ly$α$ AP measurement, DESI provides its most precise anchor for the expansion history at $z > 1$ in the matter-dominated Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Alcock-Paczyński (AP) measurements from the full shape of Lyman-α forest correlation functions in DESI DR2, achieving 1% precision at z_eff=2.33. Combined with BAO, it yields precise constraints on D_H/r_d and D_M/r_d, a Hubble constant H0=66.5±1.3, and a matter fraction Ωm=0.325±0.018. The new measurement slightly reduces the DESI-CMB discrepancy from 2.4σ to 2.2σ and supports time-evolving dark energy (w0, wa) at 2.7–3.2σ with external data.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to provide a precise Alcock-Paczyński (AP) measurement from the full shape of the Lyα forest correlation functions in DESI DR2 to constrain the expansion history at high redshift (z>1), complementing BAO constraints and testing cosmological models, particularly dark energy.
AI.method: The authors measure the AP effect from the full shape of Lyα forest auto-correlation and cross-correlation with quasars using DESI DR2 data. They combine these AP results with BAO measurements from the same dataset, and fit cosmological parameters assuming ΛCDM, adding a nucleosynthesis prior and external datasets (CMB, supernovae) for extended dark energy models.
AI.result: The AP constraint reaches 1% precision at z_eff=2.33, twice as tight as the BAO-only constraint. Combined results yield D_H/r_d=8.600±0.066 and D_M/r_d=39.32±0.33, H0=66.5±1.3 (with BBN prior), and Ωm=0.325±0.018. The DESI-CMB discrepancy reduces from 2.4σ to 2.2σ, and (w0, wa) dark energy models are preferred over ΛCDM at 2.7σ (DESI+CMB) and 3.2σ (including supernovae).
AI.conclusion: The Lyα AP measurement from DESI DR2 provides the most precise anchor for the expansion history at z>1, improves constraints on cosmological parameters, and slightly weakens the DESI-CMB tension while continuing to support evolving dark energy scenarios over ΛCDM when combined with external probes.

title: Stellar photoionisation modelling in SYNTHESIZER
comment: 29 pages and 29 figures. Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Emission from photoionised gas surrounding young stellar populations ($H\text{II}$ regions) provides critical diagnostics of the physical conditions in star forming galaxies. This emission constrains the gas properties, the nature of ionising sources, and generates essential features for determining galaxy redshifts. To leverage spectroscopic observations to test galaxy formation models, it is essential to incorporate these emissions into synthetic datasets. Here, we present the integration of photoionised gas emission into the SYNTHESIZER package (https://synthesizer-project.github.io) and demonstrate its application. We quantify the impact of key modelling assumptions - including stellar population synthesis models, initial mass functions, ionisation parameter, gas density, geometry, abundance pattern, elemental depletion, and dust - on spectral diagnostics. Furthermore, we demonstrate the versatility of SYNTHESIZER through its application in different scenarios ranging from exploring emission in toy parametric models to large-volume cosmological simulations with realistic star formation and metal enrichment histories. Taken together, SYNTHESIZER provides a flexible, physically motivated framework to model stellar and nebular emissions, serving as a vital link between theory and observations in the era of next-generation spectroscopic missions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the integration of photoionised gas (nebular) emission into the SYNTHESIZER package, a Python-based framework for modelling stellar and nebular emissions from star-forming galaxies, and demonstrates its application across toy models to cosmological simulations.
AI.motivation: Emission from photoionised gas (HII regions) provides critical diagnostics for understanding physical conditions in star-forming galaxies, constraining gas properties and ionising sources, and enabling galaxy redshift determination. To leverage spectroscopic observations for testing galaxy formation models, these emissions must be incorporated into synthetic datasets.
AI.method: The authors integrated photoionised gas emission into the SYNTHESIZER package and quantified the impact of key modelling assumptions—including stellar population synthesis models, initial mass functions, ionisation parameter, gas density, geometry, abundance pattern, elemental depletion, and dust—on spectral diagnostics. Applications range from toy parametric models to large-volume cosmological simulations with realistic star formation and metal enrichment histories.
AI.result: The SYNTHESIZER package provides a flexible, physically motivated framework capable of modelling both stellar and nebular emissions, demonstrated across diverse scenarios from toy models to cosmological simulations.
AI.conclusion: SYNTHESIZER serves as a vital link between theory and observations, providing a versatile framework for modelling galaxy emissions in the era of next-generation spectroscopic missions.

title: Validation of the DESI DR2 Ly$α$ forest full-shape analysis
summary: We present the validation of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2) Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest full-shape analysis. This analysis combines three-dimensional Ly$α$ forest auto-correlations and cross-correlations with quasars to extract information from both the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature and the broadband clustering signal, with primary emphasis on the Alcock-Paczynski (AP) measurement. Compared to the DESI DR1 analysis, the DR2 validation uses substantially larger and more realistic mock datasets, including CoLoRe 2LPT and AbacusSummit Ly$α$ forest simulations. The modeling framework is also improved through analytic marginalization over small scales ($<10$ $h^{-1}$Mpc) and the impact of ultraviolet background fluctuations. The validation program was completed prior to unblinding and defines quantitative requirements for the cosmological parameters of interest, which are evaluated using hundreds of mock realizations. We further test the analysis through independent fits to the auto- and cross-correlations, multiple catalog splits, and a broad suite of analysis and modeling variations applied to both mocks and blinded observational data. We find that the BAO and AP parameters satisfy all validation requirements and remain stable across all tests. In contrast, mock studies reveal a significant bias in the inferred growth-rate parameter $fσ_8$, leading us to exclude this measurement from the final analysis. The consistency across mocks, data splits, and robustness tests demonstrates that the DR2 Ly$α$ full-shape analysis provides a reliable and substantially improved broadband AP measurement over previous Ly$α$ forest studies.

AI.tldr: This paper validates the DESI DR2 Lyman-$\\alpha$ forest full-shape analysis, which combines 3D auto- and cross-correlations with quasars to extract BAO and broadband clustering information (emphasizing the Alcock-Paczynski measurement). Using substantially larger and more realistic mocks (CoLoRe 2LPT and AbacusSummit), improved modeling with analytic small-scale marginalization and UV background fluctuation handling, the validation confirms BAO and AP parameters satisfy all requirements and are stable across extensive tests, but reveals a significant bias in $f\\sigma_8$, excluding it from the final analysis.
AI.motivation: To rigorously validate the DESI DR2 Lyman-$\\alpha$ forest full-shape analysis prior to unblinding, ensuring the cosmological parameter measurements (BAO, AP, growth rate) are unbiased and reliable through extensive mock-based testing and robustness checks.
AI.method: The validation employs hundreds of mock realizations from larger and more realistic simulations (CoLoRe 2LPT and AbacusSummit Ly$\\alpha$ forest mocks), an improved modeling framework with analytic marginalization over scales $<10$ $h^{-1}$Mpc and UV background fluctuations, independent fits to auto- and cross-correlations, catalog splits, and a broad suite of analysis and modeling variations applied to both mocks and blinded observational data.
AI.result: BAO and AP parameters pass all quantitative validation requirements and remain stable across all tests (mocks, data splits, robustness variations). However, mock studies reveal a significant bias in the growth-rate parameter $f\\sigma_8$, leading to its exclusion from the final analysis.
AI.conclusion: The DESI DR2 Ly$\\alpha$ full-shape analysis provides a reliable and substantially improved broadband AP measurement compared to previous Ly$\\alpha$ forest studies, with consistency demonstrated across mocks, data splits, and robustness tests, while the $f\\sigma_8$ measurement is not released due to identified bias.

title: Galactic HII regions in LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae
comment: 21 pages, 13 figures, accepted by AJ
summary: Based on LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N) data and WISE Galactic HII region catalog, we construct a sample of 280 Galactic HII regions and candidates in the Outer Galaxy (80$^{\circ}$ $\lesssim$ l $\lesssim$ 220$^{\circ}$). Using MRS-N optical spectra, we measure four emission lines (H$α$, [NII]$λ$6584, [SII]$λλ$6717,6731) and use line-ratios to spectroscopically confirm 255 HII regions, including 90 previously "Known" HII regions and 165 newly classified ones. We measure their $T_{\rm e}$, $n_{\rm e}$ and oxygen abundance, and determine distances via associated OB stars and the kinematic method. The sample spans $R_{\rm gal}$ from 8.16 to 15.36 kpc, enabling investigation of radial gradients in physical properties. We find [NII]/H$α$ and [SII]/H$α$ decrease with increasing $R_{\rm gal}$, while [SII]/[NII] remains nearly flat; these trends are quite different from diffuse ionized gas (DIG). We derive the $T_{\rm e}$ gradient of 344.530 $\pm$ 78.083 K kpc$^{-1}$, and the $\log n_{\rm e}$ gradient of -0.143 $\pm$ 0.041 cm$^{-3}$ kpc$^{-1}$. Oxygen abundance shows a steep slope of -0.044 $\pm$ 0.010 dex kpc$^{-1}$ in the inner disk and a shallow slope of -0.016 $\pm$ 0.005 dex kpc$^{-1}$ in the outer disk, with a global slope of -0.014 $\pm$ 0.005 dex kpc$^{-1}$. We also examine the two-dimensional distributions of $T_{\rm e}$, $n_{\rm e}$, and oxygen abundance, and find the gradients vary with azimuth. There is no obvious difference between spiral arm and interarm regions, and no trend appears along individual arms. From [NII]/H$α$-[SII]$λ$6717/H$α$ diagram, HII regions have a S$^+$/S ratio (0.32), lower than DIG (0.43); however, heavy overlap prevents clear separation from this diagram alone.

AI.tldr: Using LAMOST MRS-N optical spectra and WISE Galactic HII region catalog, the authors spectroscopically confirm 255 of 280 Galactic HII regions and candidates in the Outer Galaxy (l = 80°-220°). They measure electron temperature, density, and oxygen abundance, derive radial gradients across R_gal = 8.16-15.36 kpc, and examine 2D azimuthal variations. Key findings include a positive T_e gradient, negative n_e gradient, steep-then-shallow oxygen abundance gradient (broken slope), and line-ratio trends distinct from diffuse ionized gas.
AI.motivation: To construct a large, spectroscopically confirmed sample of Galactic HII regions in the Outer Galaxy and use it to investigate radial gradients of physical properties (temperature, density, oxygen abundance) and their dependence on azimuth and spiral structure, thereby extending our understanding of Galactic chemical and physical evolution beyond the solar circle.
AI.method: Cross-match LAMOST MRS-N (Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae) data with the WISE Galactic HII region catalog to build a sample of 280 HII regions in the Outer Galaxy. Use MRS-N optical spectra to measure Hα, [NII]6584, and [SII]6717,6731 emission lines. Apply line-ratio diagnostics to spectroscopically confirm 255 HII regions. Measure T_e, n_e, and oxygen abundance, and determine distances via associated OB stars and kinematic methods. Perform radial gradient analysis, 2D distribution mapping, and spiral arm/interarm comparisons.
AI.result: 255 HII regions confirmed (90 known + 165 newly classified). [NII]/Hα and [SII]/Hα decrease with R_gal while [SII]/[NII] stays flat—distinct from DIG. T_e gradient = 344.530 ± 78.083 K/kpc; log n_e gradient = -0.143 ± 0.041 cm^-3/kpc. Oxygen abundance shows a broken gradient: steep inner slope (-0.044 dex/kpc) and shallow outer slope (-0.016 dex/kpc), with a global slope of -0.014 dex/kpc. Gradients vary with azimuth; no spiral arm/interarm difference or intra-arm trends. HII regions have S+/S ratio of 0.32 (lower than DIG's 0.43) but heavy overlap prevents clear separation.
AI.conclusion: The Outer Galaxy HII region sample reveals significant radial gradients in physical properties that differ from the solar neighborhood, including a broken oxygen abundance gradient and distinct line-ratio behavior compared to diffuse ionized gas. The azimuthal variation of gradients and lack of spiral arm contrast suggest that additional factors beyond spiral structure shape the chemical and physical state of the outer Galactic disk.

title: CoLoRe-2LPT: Lyman-$α$ mock catalogues for the validation of DESI cosmological analyses
comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables. Plan to submit to A&A
summary: The Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest has become a crucial probe for studying the large-scale structure of the universe at high redshift ($z > 2$), providing powerful constraints on Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) and the full-shape (FS) clustering of matter. As a key ingredient for upcoming BAO and FS analyses, we present a new generation of fast cosmological Ly$α$ mocks based on second-order Lagrangian perturbation theory (2LPT). These new mocks significantly improve upon previous log-normal approaches, both at accurately capturing small scale clustering and at recovering the non-linear broadening of the BAO peak. They are able to reproduce Ly$α$ statistics within $10\%$ of the latest DESI measurement; including the Ly$α$ bias and the redshift-space distortion $β$ parameter, mean transmitted flux, and 1D power spectrum. The corresponding quasar (QSO) clustering is also improved with respect to previous approaches, calibrated against high-resolution Abacus simulations, recovering the observational QSO linear bias to less than $5\%$ and improving redshift-space distortions via 2LPT velocities and the addition of Fingers-of-God effects. Furthermore, these mocks incorporate high column density systems and metal lines, allowing us to explore the effects and systematics induced by these astrophysical contaminants. This new set of mocks has been key for enhancing the modeling and validation of the DESI DR2 Ly$α$ full shape cosmological analysis. This work provides a physically motivated and computationally efficient tool for simulating current and next-generation Ly$α$ surveys and validating FS and BAO analysis.

These mocks accurately reproduce Lyα statistics within 10% of DESI measurements (bias, redshift-space distortion β, mean transmitted flux, 1D power spectrum), improve QSO clustering with calibrated bias within 5%, and incorporate astrophysical contaminants like high column density systems and metal lines. They were key for validating the DESI DR2 Lyα full-shape cosmological analysis.
AI.motivation: Upcoming BAO and full-shape analyses of the Lyα forest require fast and accurate mocks that capture small-scale clustering and non-linear BAO peak broadening, which previous log-normal mock approaches failed to reproduce accurately.
AI.method: The mocks are generated using second-order Lagrangian perturbation theory (2LPT), which improves over log-normal methods. QSO clustering is calibrated against high-resolution Abacus simulations, with 2LPT velocities and Fingers-of-God effects for improved redshift-space distortions. The mocks also incorporate high column density systems and metal lines to study astrophysical contaminants.
AI.result: The new mocks reproduce Lyα statistics within 10% of the latest DESI measurements, recover the observational QSO linear bias to less than 5%, and improve upon previous log-normal approaches in both small-scale clustering and non-linear BAO peak broadening.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a physically motivated and computationally efficient tool for simulating current and next-generation Lyα surveys, crucial for validating FS and BAO cosmological analyses.

title: The X-ray-Weak Tail of the Quasar Population: Physical Properties and Redshift Evolution of Variability-Selected AGN in eFEDS
comment: Submitted to A&A
summary: (abridged) Aims: To characterize variability-selected AGN candidates within the eROSITA Final Equatorial-Depth Survey (eFEDS), leveraging the synergy between optical variability and deep X-ray observations by SRG (Spectrum Roentgen Gamma)/eROSITA, to compare the physical properties of AGN populations selected through complementary methods. Methods: We used a sample of AGN candidates selected via optical variability by Arévalo et al. and cross-match it to the X-ray selected eFEDS AGN sample. Spectroscopic characterizations are obtained for the matched samples from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument public data products. Results: We find a high classification purity with 98% candidates confirmed as broad-line AGN/QSOs. We identify a significant population (25%) that lack X-ray counterparts (X-U) in the eFEDS survey. We find that the X-D and X-U samples exhibit distinct physical properties and redshift distributions. The X-U sample peaks at $z = 2$ while the X-D sample at $z =1$, with nearly half of the variability-selected AGN at $z > 2.5$ remaining undetected in X-rays. This missing fraction can be attributed to K-correction effects and SED evolution with luminosity, mainly resulting in high accretion rate objects falling out of the X-D sample at higher redshifts. X-ray variability accounts for a part of the missing fraction but its dependence with redshift is less clear. Ensemble spectral analysis reveals that X-D sources have steeper optical continua and stronger broad emission lines than their X-U counterparts, while the forbidden and semi-forbidden lines have equal EWs in both samples. Finally, broad absorption line (BAL) features are found almost exclusively in the X-U population. This "missing" X-ray population must be accounted for when extrapolating X-ray-selected AGN to the broader Type I population and could impact cosmic estimates of massive black hole growth.

These X-ray-undetected (X-U) sources peak at z=2 (vs z=1 for X-ray-detected) and are missed due to K-correction effects, SED evolution, and possibly X-ray variability. X-U sources have flatter optical continua and weaker broad emission lines, and BAL features appear almost exclusively in this population, with implications for cosmic black hole growth estimates.
AI.motivation: To exploit the synergy between optical variability selection and deep eROSITA X-ray observations to characterize AGN populations selected through complementary methods, particularly to understand populations missed by X-ray selection and their implications for the broader Type I AGN population and black hole growth estimates.
AI.method: Cross-matching optical variability-selected AGN candidates (from Arévalo et al.) to the X-ray selected eFEDS AGN sample, using spectroscopic characterization from Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) public data products, including ensemble spectral analysis.
AI.result: 98% classification purity (broad-line AGN/QSOs); 25% lack X-ray counterparts (X-U). X-U sources peak at z=2, X-D at z=1, with ~half of variability-selected AGN at z>2.5 undetected in X-rays. X-D sources have steeper optical continua and stronger broad lines; BAL features almost exclusively in X-U.
AI.conclusion: The X-ray "missing" AGN population must be accounted for when extrapolating X-ray-selected AGN to the broader Type I population, as it could significantly impact cosmic estimates of massive black hole growth.

title: Lyman-$α$ forest holography: 3D predictions from 1D measurements
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: Cosmological analyses of Lyman-$α$ forest clustering rely on either one-dimensional correlations along individual sightlines or three-dimensional correlations between different sightlines. Because these observables probe the matter distribution on very different scales, they have traditionally been analyzed independently. In this work, we bridge this gap using ForestFlow, an emulator trained on a suite of cosmological hydrodynamical simulations that provides a unified description of Lyman-$α$ forest clustering from linear to nonlinear scales. This framework enables us to determine the range of three-dimensional clustering models compatible with the DESI one-dimensional flux power spectrum ($P_{\rm 1D}$). The resulting predictions successfully reproduce the large-scale clustering measured by the DESI BAO analysis and provide physically motivated priors on nonlinear clustering that are used in a companion paper presenting the full-shape analysis of the DESI DR2 Lyman-$α$ forest. We validate our methodology using the large-volume, high-resolution hydrodynamical simulation ACCEL-2, demonstrating excellent agreement across the full range of scales considered. Finally, we combine constraints from the $P_{\rm 1D}$ and BAO analyses on the parameter combinations $b_δσ_8$ and $b_ηf σ_8$, finding that the two probes provide comparable constraining power while exhibiting complementary parameter degeneracies. Our results establish a direct connection between one- and three-dimensional Lyman-$α$ forest measurements through ForestFlow, an approach we term Lyman-$α$ holography by analogy with the reconstruction of higher-dimensional structure from lower-dimensional information.

AI.tldr: ForestFlow is an emulator trained on hydrodynamical simulations that unifies 1D and 3D Lyman-α forest clustering analyses, bridging the gap between P1D and BAO measurements using what the authors call "Lyman-α holography."
AI.motivation: Traditionally, Lyman-α forest clustering is analyzed via either 1D correlations along single sightlines or 3D correlations between different sightlines, which probe different scales and have been treated independently. This paper aims to unify these observables to extract consistent cosmological constraints.
AI.method: The authors train ForestFlow, an emulator on cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, to provide a unified description of Lyman-α forest clustering from linear to nonlinear scales. They use it to determine which 3D clustering models are compatible with DESI 1D flux power spectrum (P1D) data, validate against the ACCEL-2 simulation, and combine constraints on bδσ8 and bηfσ8 from both P1D and BAO analyses.
AI.result: The predictions reproduce large-scale clustering from DESI BAO analysis. Validation against ACCEL-2 shows excellent agreement across all scales. Combined constraints from P1D and BAO on bδσ8 and bηfσ8 show comparable constraining power with complementary parameter degeneracies.
AI.conclusion: ForestFlow establishes a direct connection between 1D and 3D Lyman-α forest measurements, enabling physically motivated priors on nonlinear clustering for full-shape analysis of DESI DR2 data, a method termed "Lyman-α holography."

title: Revealing the Physical Driver of the Baldwin Effect: Gas Density in the Broad-Line Region
comment: Comments: 11 pages, 7 figures, 4 appendix figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The Baldwin effect --- the inverse correlation between the equivalent width of emission lines and the continuum luminosity in active galactic nuclei (AGNs) --- has been known for nearly five decades, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. Using a sample of 41,159 radio quasars constructed from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and the Low-Frequency Array Two-metre Sky Survey, we investigate the origin and underlying physics of the Baldwin effect of MgII broad emission lines in both radio-quiet (RQ) and radio-loud (RL) quasars. We find that the slope $β$ of the Baldwin effect is positively correlated with the Eddington ratio $λ_{\rm Edd}$ in both populations, and RL quasars exhibit steeper $β$ than their RQ quasars at fixed $λ_{\rm Edd}$. Photoionization simulations reveal that the $β$ is primarily governed by the gas density in the broad-line region (BLR): lower gas densities yield steeper slopes. This density-driven mechanism naturally connects the Baldwin effect to the broader AGN evolutionary context. Specifically, higher $λ_{\rm Edd}$ drive stronger accretion disk winds, leading to denser BLRs and shallower $β$. Our findings indicate that BLR gas density serves as the primary physical driver underlying the "global" Baldwin effect, offering a physically grounded framework for interpreting AGN accretion states and their coupled evolution with host galaxies.

AI.tldr: This study uses 41,159 radio quasars from SDSS and LoTSS to investigate the physical origin of the MgII Baldwin effect. The slope β is positively correlated with Eddington ratio (λ_Edd) in both radio-quiet and radio-loud quasars, with radio-loud objects showing steeper slopes at fixed λ_Edd. Photoionization simulations show β is primarily governed by broad-line region (BLR) gas density, where lower densities yield steeper slopes. This density-driven mechanism links the Baldwin effect to AGN evolution via accretion disk winds.
AI.motivation: The Baldwin effect has been known for nearly five decades, but its physical origin remains poorly understood. This work aims to uncover the underlying physics and connect it to the broader AGN evolutionary framework.
AI.method: The authors construct a sample of 41,159 radio quasars from SDSS and LoTTS, compare the Baldwin effect slope β for MgII in radio-quiet and radio-loud quasars, correlate β with Eddington ratio, and use photoionization simulations to test the role of BLR gas density as the governing physical parameter.
AI.result: The Baldwin effect slope β positively correlates with Eddington ratio in both RQ and RL quasars, with RL objects showing steeper slopes at fixed λ_Edd. Photoionization simulations reveal β is primarily set by BLR gas density, with lower densities producing steeper slopes. Higher λ_Edd drive stronger disk winds, yielding denser BLRs and shallower β.
AI.conclusion: BLR gas density is the primary physical driver of the "global" Baldwin effect, providing a physically grounded framework linking the Baldwin effect to AGN accretion states and host galaxy co-evolution.

title: Unified dark sector approaches to cosmological tensions
comment: 28 pages, 6 figures
summary: We present an analytical study of minimal mass-varying dark matter models, in which a single scalar field controls the dark matter mass, focusing on their utility in simultaneously addressing multiple cosmological tensions. We show that such minimal models can naturally become relevant at two critical epochs in the history of the Universe; matter-radiation equality and the present day, generating an early dark energy-like energy injection, as motivated by the Hubble tension, and an apparent phantom crossing, as suggested by baryon acoustic oscillation data from the DESI project. Crucially, the characteristic timing of these effects is tied to the cosmological background evolution itself, rather than specific energy scales. In addition, the intermediate evolution reduces the clustering matter density and can therefore lower $S_8$, in the direction preferred by data, while avoiding new long-range interactions. We derive analytic arguments to understand the conditions for these effects to arise in the same model and assess whether they can occur without introducing additional fine-tuning. This provides a simple framework for identifying which potentials and couplings to dark matter can simultaneously affect early- and late-time cosmological tensions.

AI.method: The paper presents an analytical study of mass-varying dark matter models where a single scalar field controls the dark matter mass. The authors derive analytic arguments for the conditions under which these effects arise in the same model and assess whether they can occur without introducing additional fine-tuning.
AI.result: The analysis shows that minimal mass-varying dark matter models can naturally become relevant at two critical epochs—matter-radiation equality and present day—generating early dark energy-like injection and apparent phantom crossing respectively. The characteristic timing is tied to cosmological background evolution rather than specific energy scales, and the intermediate evolution reduces clustering matter density, lowering S8 in the direction preferred by data, while avoiding new long-range interactions.

title: The eROSITA X-ray luminosity function of active galactic nuclei
comment: 25 pages, 15 figures. Catalogue including redshift information is released via the eROSITA web pages and CDS upon the journal's article acceptance
summary: The X-ray luminosity function (XLF) of active galactic nuclei (AGN) provides an observational probe of the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) across cosmic time. With its large survey grasp, Spectrum Roentgen Gamma (SRG)/eROSITA samples the luminosity--redshift plane with a depth--area balance complementary to pencil-beam surveys, providing the volume needed to detect rare luminous AGN, previously limited by small-number statistics. We measure the soft XLF, leveraging an eROSITA sample spanning approximately eight orders of magnitude in luminosity out to $z\simeq6$. This enables us to study luminosity-dependent evolution with improved constraints, and to infer both the SMBH accretion history and optical/UV missed AGN population. We introduce a new redshift-dependent smoothly broken power-law parameterisation in which all XLF model parameters are allowed to evolve continuously with redshift. We find lower space densities for moderately and very luminous AGN at low redshift, while the abundance is higher than previously found at the highest redshifts. Comparisons to optical/UV quasar LFs converted to rest-frame $2\!-\!10\,\mathrm{keV}$ show that the UV-missed fraction decreases with luminosity, and, in the most luminous bin, increases with redshift. Integrating the XLF yields a black-hole accretion-rate density peaking at $z \simeq 1.5$, with the corresponding cumulative black-hole mass density indicating $\sim80^{+11}_{-23}\%$ obscured growth relative to locally-inferred BH mass estimates derived from scaling relations and missed by the soft X-ray selection of our sample. With this work, we release the eROSITA DR2 AGN catalogue, including counterparts and their redshift information. We then discuss how these results can inform future spectroscopic, photometric, and X-ray survey strategies aimed at improving AGN demographic constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new measurement of the soft X-ray luminosity function (XLF) of AGN using eROSITA data (SRG) spanning ~8 orders of magnitude in luminosity out to z≃6, with a new redshift-dependent smoothly broken power-law parameterization. The authors find lower space densities for moderately/luminous AGN at low redshift but higher densities at high redshift, quantify the UV-missed AGN fraction, and infer that ~80% of SMBH growth is obscured relative to local estimates. They also release the eROSITA DR2 AGN catalogue.
AI.motivation: To overcome small-number statistics that previously limited measurements of rare luminous AGN, and to improve constraints on luminosity-dependent AGN evolution, SMBH accretion history, and the optically/UV-missed AGN population using eROSITA's large survey area with complementary depth-area balance.
AI.method: The authors measure the soft XLF from an eROSITA sample covering ~8 decades in luminosity to z~6, introducing a new redshift-dependent smoothly broken power-law parameterization in which all XLF model parameters evolve continuously with redshift. They compare to optical/UV quasar luminosity functions converted to rest-frame 2-10 keV, and integrate the XLF to derive the black-hole accretion-rate density and cumulative black-hole mass density.
AI.result: Lower space densities are found for moderately and very luminous AGN at low redshift, while abundances are higher than previously found at the highest redshifts. The UV-missed fraction decreases with luminosity and increases with redshift in the most luminous bin. The BH accretion-rate density peaks at z~1.5, and ~80% of growth is obscured relative to local BH mass estimates. The eROSITA DR2 AGN catalogue is released.
AI.conclusion: The improved XLF constraints from eROSITA reveal redshift- and luminosity-dependent AGN evolution that differs from previous findings, highlight substantial obscured SMBH growth missed by soft X-ray selection, and inform future spectroscopic, photometric, and X-ray survey strategies for better AGN demographic constraints.

title: A study of the large-scale formation in the environment of A3266: Infalling groups, filaments, and a premerger cold front
comment: 10 pages and 13 figures in the main text plus 2 pages and 2 figures as appendix. Astronomy & Astrophysics, accepted on June 29, 2026
summary:
Abell 3266 (A3266) is a dynamically active galaxy cluster embedded in a dense environment of galaxy groups and clusters at similar redshift. Data from the Spektrum Roentgen Gamma (SRG)/eROSITA all-sky survey enable the study of faint X-ray emission in cluster outskirts.
  We investigate the previously unexplored outskirts of A3266 out to $3R_{100}$, characterize its nearest neighboring galaxy group, and search for connecting filaments using X-ray emission and galaxy number density.
  We performed X-ray imaging, surface brightness, and spectral analyses in selected regions and sectors. These were complemented by the distribution of member galaxies from the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database NED and by comparison with the cosmological simulation Simulating the LOcal Web (SLOW).
  We detect an X-ray filament connecting A3266 to its nearest northwestern group over a 3D length of $L_{R_{200}\text{--}R_{200}} = {1.1}_{-0.1}^{+0.5},\mathrm{Mpc}$ with a significance of $3.6,σ$. The group exhibits cool-core properties and is embedded within the filament. The filament has a temperature of $T={1.2}_{-0.2}^{+0.3},\mathrm{keV}$, metallicity $Z={0.07}_{-0.05}^{+0.09},Z{\odot}$, and, assuming a simple geometry, an electron number density of $n_{\rm e}={8}_{-2}^{+1}\times 10^{-5},\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$.
  Our findings reveal a coherent network of galaxy groups around A3266, tracing its ongoing assembly along the large-scale structure. The filament is hotter and denser than expected for pristine warm-hot intergalactic medium, consistent with gas processed in the cluster environment and influenced by the infall of the northwestern group. Comparison with SLOW shows that the observed group distribution and filamentary connections are qualitatively consistent with an actively accreting cluster embedded in the cosmic web.

The filament is hotter and denser than pristine warm-hot intergalactic medium, consistent with cluster-processed gas, and the observed group distribution agrees qualitatively with simulations of an actively accreting cluster embedded in the cosmic web.
AI.motivation: To investigate the previously unexplored outskirts of the dynamically active galaxy cluster A3266, characterize its nearest neighboring galaxy group, and search for connecting filaments—thereby probing cluster formation and gas processing in the cosmic web.
AI.method: The study combines X-ray imaging, surface brightness, and spectral analyses in selected regions and sectors using SRG/eROSITA data, complemented by member galaxy distributions from NED and comparison with the SLOW cosmological simulation.
AI.result: An X-ray filament connecting A3266 to its northwestern group is detected over L_R200–R200 = 1.1 Mpc (3.6σ), with T ≈ 1.2 keV, Z ≈ 0.07 Z⊙, and ne ≈ 8×10^-5 cm^-3. The group is a cool-core system embedded within the filament. The filament is hotter and denser than expected for pristine WHIM.
